clue.text: Take a tray out to Lois, working alone

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of tray and Lois are put out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to carry a tray out to Lois, who is working by herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TRAY plus LOIS; 'Take a', 'to' and 'working' are surface padding, though 'working' also hints at the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary describes being on one's own, without company, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A very good head for business — wonderful

parts.note: something very good is super, a straightforward synonym

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of business

explanation.surface: A fine business leader is praised as wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is an everyday synonym for excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Catch half of your fish using bait

indicators.note: the fish catches, or holds within it, the other piece

parts.note: the ling is a long food fish of the cod family

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two letters; here the latter pair of your

explanation.surface: An angler is told to keep half of the fish caught by baiting the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of your' gives UR, which LING catches to make L-UR-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Luring means enticing or tempting, exactly what using bait does.

clue.text: Full information about a hundred robberies

indicators.note: about means placed around, so robberies wraps the other pieces

parts.note: robberies are thefts
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A police report gives the complete details of a hundred burglaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The full information on a matter is the whole truth of it, as in 'give me the details'.

clue.text: Right ear's back

parts.note: the word ear as written, the possessive adding nothing

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's right ear is at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear is the back part of something, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Goes beyond advances

definitions.meaning: to go beyond is to overtake or exceed, as one car does another
advances here are amorous approaches, as in making a pass at someone

explanation.definitionFit: Passing means overtaking, and a pass is also a romantic or sexual advance.

clue.text: Although getting ahead, it's not for long

parts.note: read as a head: the letter A goes at the front
while can mean although, as in 'while I agree, I doubt it'

explanation.surface: A remark that though someone is getting ahead, it will not last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' splits into 'a head': an A placed at the head of WHILE; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: For a short time is the meaning of this adverb, as in 'wait for a short period'.

clue.text: Yelled driving too fast

definitions.meaning: to yell is to shriek or cry out loudly
a speeding car is said to tear or roar along, moving with a high-pitched engine noise

explanation.definitionFit: To scream is to shriek, and informally a car that speeds past is said to scream along the road.

clue.text: Lovely girl from a TV serial seen in bathroom

indicators.note: from places the piece named first after what follows, as one piece taken from the other

parts.note: a soap opera is a long-running TV serial
an attractive person is informally called a dish

explanation.surface: A beautiful actress from a television serial is spotted in a bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade reads backwards: DISH comes from SOAP, so SOAP goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tray for holding soap is a fixture found by a basin or bath.

clue.text: As usual, the name's misspelt. It's Italian

parts.note: par is the usual or normal standard, as in 'par for the course'

indicators.note: misspelt means the letters of name's are written in a wrong order

parts.note: the word name with its S, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A complaint that, as always, someone's name has been spelt wrongly, as it is Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: This cheese is from Parma, and the word also describes things from that Italian city.

clue.text: A phrase translated from the Himalayan

indicators.note: translated suggests the word phrase is turned into a different form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A phrase rendered into English from a language of the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherpas are a people of the Himalayas in Nepal, famed as mountain guides.

clue.text: Gave answer to "Will you return to ferrying?"

definitions.meaning: to give an answer to is to respond
plied once more, as a ferry plies a route again

explanation.definitionFit: Replied means answered or responded, and split it reads as plied again.

clue.text: Fugitive lost article at the airport

indicators.note: lost means a piece is dropped from the word for fugitive

parts.note: a fugitive is a runaway
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An escaped prisoner left an item of luggage behind at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found at the airport: the strip where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: A beautifully enunciated "Hear, hear!"

definitions.meaning: spoken clearly and finely, words delivered well
an expression of agreement with a speaker

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes good speech and is also a cry of approval meaning 'just so'.

clue.text: Urging dog to climb in

indicators.note: in places the climbing word inside the dog

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
to shin up is to climb using arms and legs

explanation.surface: Someone encourages a dog to clamber in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing means pressing or urging someone to act.

clue.text: How the decision not to slim was defended?

definitions.text: How the decision not to slim was defended?

parts.words: How the decision not to slim was defended?
parts.note: someone who refuses to slim chooses to stay fat, and defends that choice resolutely, in a manner that matches their figure

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means resolutely or firmly, and its root also means plump.

clue.text: Understands when you say "Confiscate"

indicators.note: spoken words are signalled, so the sound of the word for confiscate counts

parts.note: to confiscate is to seize

explanation.surface: Someone grasps a point the moment you say the word confiscate.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp or understand it, as in 'I see'.

clue.text: Weapon of the angry actor at curtain-call?

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
an actor at the curtain-call bends forward to acknowledge applause

explanation.surface: Wondering what weapon a furious performer would carry when taking applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow mounted on a stock, firing bolts.

clue.text: Found how to translate "does unto"

indicators.note: translate suggests the letters of does unto are rendered into new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovered the meaning of the biblical 'does unto'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosed out means discovered or found by searching, like a sniffing dog.

clue.text: Inflammation from user in it

indicators.note: from indicates the answer is made out of these letters, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor says the inflammation came from a user being involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuritis is the medical term for swelling of a nerve, a kind of inflammation.

clue.text: Nothing in bar measure

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is measured in the pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is an old unit of land area, a quarter of an acre.

clue.text: Bucked when roared out

definitions.meaning: bucked up means heartened or encouraged
shouted approval loudly, as a crowd does

explanation.definitionFit: To be cheered is to be heartened, and to cheer is to shout approval.

clue.text: Three times an hour in an instant

indicators.note: in places the hour's abbreviation inside the instant

parts.note: in a trice means in an instant

explanation.surface: Something happens three times an hour, each in a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrice is an old word meaning on three occasions.

clue.text: Give name as Capone that's the password

parts.note: to sign is to write one's name
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster film line: give your name as Capone and that gets you in.
explanation.definitionFit: A password is a secret sign or cue that grants entry, a kind of signal.

clue.text: Left among GBS's items of clothing

indicators.note: among places the letter for left inside the playwright's possessive

parts.note: GBS is George Bernard Shaw, so his is Shaw's

explanation.surface: Something left among George Bernard Shaw's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shawls are wraps worn round the shoulders, so garments.

clue.text: Understand an article and become furious

definitions.note: a verb phrase where the answer is the present participle, being furious

parts.note: to see is to understand
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: Someone grasps a newspaper article and flies into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil with rage; seething is that state of fury.

clue.text: A shadow of one's former self!

definitions.text: A shadow of one's former self!

parts.words: A shadow of one's former self!
parts.note: taken literally, a shadowy figure of someone who has died, a ghost rather than a weakened person

explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost or spectral apparition, a pale shade of the dead.

clue.text: Heavens, be off with you and say no more!

annotationWithheld.why: Heavens, be off with you and say no more! (4) for JOSH: the pieces give GOSH, SHOO or HUSH, nothing builds J-O-S-H and no word defines tease; clue appears to belong elsewhere or be garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Heavens, be off with you and say no more!

clue.text: How the blasted unexpected guests arrive?

definitions.text: How the blasted unexpected guests arrive?

parts.words: How the blasted unexpected guests arrive?
parts.note: visitors who turn up out of the blue, pictured as if a gale carried them in

explanation.definitionFit: To blow in is an idiom for arriving casually or unexpectedly.

clue.text: Can't say-haven't been introduced

definitions.meaning: unable to answer, having no idea

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for being unsure, and also for not being acquainted with someone.

clue.text: Having returned, fade

annotationWithheld.why: Having returned, fade (6) for WITHER: Having gives WITH, but no word supplies ER; the clue appears cut short in the OCR

clue.text: Sounds that provoke the "Shut up, boy!"

definitions.text: Sounds that provoke the "Shut up, boy!"

parts.words: Sounds that provoke the "Shut up, boy!"
parts.note: the shrill notes a cheeky lad makes with his lips that annoy adults into telling him to be quiet

explanation.definitionFit: Whistles are high-pitched sounds made by blowing through pursed lips.
